---
title: "x[-which(...)] wipes everything when nothing matches"
ref: LEN-04
categories: [Empty and NA]
impact: silencieux
extrait: '(1:3)[-which(1:3 > 10)]'
attendu: "the whole of `x`, since there is nothing to remove"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
x <- c(a = 1, b = 2, c = 3)
x[-which(x > 2)]
x[-which(x > 10)]
```
:::

## Why

`which()` returns the positions where the condition is true. When no value meets it, it returns `integer(0)`. But `-integer(0)` is still `integer(0)`, and indexing by an empty vector selects nothing.

The code works as long as there is something to remove. The day the data is clean, it deletes everything.

## The remedy

Index with the negated logical vector, which keeps everything when no value needs excluding.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
x[!(x > 10)]
x[!(x > 2)]
```
:::
